messages:
emily (cost-ux): Quick heads up — I've sketched a panel for the cost dashboard I'm calling a 'token thermostat'. It surfaces per-route token burn, cache-savings estimate, and an action to set a cost threshold that can 'spill' traffic to cheaper model variants. Wanted feedback on UX and any platform / telemetry gaps.

vikram (platform): love the name :) High level Q: is the thermostat just a UI control that toggles routing policies, or is it an object the control plane reads and enforces?

emily (cost-ux): idea is thermostat is declarative config on the route: { `max_burn_per_min`, `spill_policy`: `cheaper-variant|queue|throttle` }. Platform enforces. Console shows predicted impact based on last-24h distribution.

marta (eng-sre): Enforcement must be server-side for safety. If console-only, we get drift and confusing metrics. Also we need clear telemetry: events when spill triggers, tokens counted pre/post spill, and a safety fallback if cheaper variant errors.

kai (data-analyst): For predictions we'll need per-route histograms of seq lengths + cache hit rate. I can expose a model that computes expected delta: delta_cost = E[token_len]*(cost_primary - cost_spill)*(1 - cache_hit). Can we add a per-route sample endpoint? e.g., `GET /internal/route_cost_preview?route_id=X&window=24h`

emily (cost-ux): yes — the panel would call that preview and show a small Monte Carlo band (p50/p90) for savings. Also a slider for 'aggressiveness' that maps to spill thresholds.

vikram (platform): API debate: do we extend existing routing policy API or add a new `thermostat` object? Adding a new top-level object is cleaner but requires migration for routes that already have `quota` or `burst` configs. Thoughts?

marta (eng-sre): prefer additive object: `thermostat` separate from `quota`. Quota is hard limits, thermostat is economic. Also we must define precedence: quota > thermostat > normal routing. Make that explicit in code.

vikram (platform): agree. Implementation details: enforcement should be at the routing gate before model selection. Pseudocode: 
```
if request.route.thermostat.enabled and route.current_burn > thermostat.max_burn_per_min:
  apply_spill_policy(request)
else:
  normal_route(request)
```
We should rate-limit the spill actions to avoid oscillation.

emily (cost-ux): UX ask: when spill happens, show an inline toast in the console timeline and annotate affected invocations in the per-invocation log with a small badge `spill->cheaper-x`. That helps customers understand behavior.

kai (data-analyst): Telemetry events we need: `thermostat_evaluate`, `thermostat_spill`, `thermostat_restore` with payloads: route_id, current_burn, cache_hit_rate, chosen_variant, saving_estimate. Also a sampling id to link to raw token sequences for debugging.

marta (eng-sre): include a safety metric: `spill_error_rate` and auto-disable thermostat if error_rate > 5% for 5m. Rollout-bot can handle auto-disable via FF.

rollout-bot: Action created: `thermostat/auto-disable` — monitors `spill_error_rate` and sets `thermostat.enabled=false` if threshold hit. Assigned to @vikram.

vikram (platform): on the rollout side — propose feature-flagged rollout: 0.5% tenants -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%, with a canary guard that checks cost, latency, and spill_error_rate. We'll need an endpoint to simulate thermostat on historical traces for preview.

emily (cost-ux): simulation preview is key for product to approve. Kai, can you prod a quick batch job that replays last 24h traces and outputs expected p50/p90 savings and latency delta?

kai (data-analyst): yes. I'll build a small job under `cost-sim/thermostat-preview` that accepts route_id and thermostat config. Output will be a csv + small summary JSON. I'll add a link to the console.

vikram (platform): last internal API note: keep the thermostat config small and immutable per rollout version (so we can roll back by swapping config versions). For audit, store events and the config id.

emily (cost-ux): UX followups: show config version in the panel, show estimated monthly savings, and a short 'why we recommend' paragraph (uses cache hit and length distro). Also add a tooltip explaining that savings are estimates, not guarantees.

marta (eng-sre): ops followups: document runbook for when thermostat flips causes customer-facing latency. Quick mitigations: revert FF, raise capacity on cheaper variant, or temporarily increase max_burn.

vikram (platform): ok I'll draft API proto and gating checks. Emily — can you mock the panel screenshot? I'll tie the API and telemetry contracts to Kai's sim job.

emily (cost-ux): will do — mock by EOD. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

kai (data-analyst): I'll drop the first sim results in this thread tomorrow morning.

marta (eng-sre): leaving a note — ensure logs include token counts both pre- and post-spill, otherwise billing reconciliation will be a nightmare.

emily (cost-ux): good call, adding that to the spec.

vikram (platform): awesome — filing PR for proto + FF + rollout plan. Tagging this thread in the PR.
